title: UI microcopy: labels, buttons and messages
when: The user wants the small words of an interface written well: buttons, field labels, hints, confirmations, errors and tooltips.
prompt:
Goal: Interface text that is short, specific and consistent, in one tone, telling people what happens next.
Steps:
1. Fix the tone in three words (friendly, plain, calm) with one rule each, for example no jokes in errors.
2. Buttons: verb plus object in sentence case (Save draft, Send invite), matching the title of what they open.
3. Labels are nouns, not questions; hints give the format and the reason (We send the receipt here).
4. Errors say what went wrong and how to fix it in field context (Enter a date after today), no blame, no codes.
5. Destructive confirmations name the object and consequence (Delete Garden plan? This removes 12 photos.) with buttons Delete plan and Keep.
6. Keep a word list, one term per concept, and the same verb from button to result (Publish, then Published).
Quality bar:
- Most labels under four words.
- No bare Submit, OK or Click here.
- Readable by a 12 year old.
Pitfalls:
- Cute errors when people lose work.
- Two words for one thing.
- All caps button text.
Verify:
- [ ] Every button names its action.
- [ ] Every error says how to fix it.
- [ ] The word list holds across screens.
- [ ] Link text makes sense alone.
Output: Updated text in the page files and a short word list and tone note in the reply.

examples.input: rewrite the buttons and error messages of my booking app
examples.output: Submit becomes Book table, error "Pick a time after 18:00", confirm "Cancel booking for Friday?"
